title: Give every authored doc a corpus-unique doc-id

facts.note: Corpus = every authored .adoc beneath docs/, all areas including archive/, excluding generated docs/dist/. This is the primary gate: the invariant holds corpus-wide at all times.

values: duplicate doc-id reported by docs_capability validator
facts.note: Sufficient trigger on its own: fires for ANY duplicate in the corpus, including pre-existing duplicates whose attributes were not touched. Detector output (validator docs_capability) must be surfaced as an activation fact.
Optional trigger, NOT a prerequisite: these operations commonly introduce collisions, but a duplicate violates the rule regardless of which operation (if any) is in progress.
Optional trigger, NOT a prerequisite: a diff-level observer parsing :doc-id: of touched docs gives early warning; absence of an id change does not exempt an existing duplicate.

fires: Planner authors a new doc under docs/ whose :doc-id: equals one already declared elsewhere in docs/.
Planner archives a doc and writes its replacement with the same :doc-id: as the archived copy in docs/archive/.
Planner copies an existing .adoc as a template and keeps its :doc-id: unchanged.
A corpus validation (or a body-only edit / move of an unrelated doc) surfaces two existing docs that already share a :doc-id:, even though neither id was changed in this task.
doesNotFire: Generated output beneath docs/dist/ shares an id with an authored doc.
An authored doc under docs/ declares no :doc-id: at all (that is planner.docs.identity-required).
Edits to a doc's body when every :doc-id: in the corpus is unique.

given: The docs/ corpus: every authored .adoc, archive/ included, docs/dist/ excluded.
when: Any declared `:doc-id:` is shared by another doc — newly introduced (create, copy, move, archive) or pre-existing and found by validation.
then: Ensure no two authored documents in the corpus declare the same `:doc-id:`.
prefer: Archived and replacement docs get DIFFERENT ids; the new one (`:status: current`) declares `:supersedes: <archived-id>`; the archived one is `:status: superseded`.
archive/ shares the id space on purpose: choose archived ids (e.g. `archive.<date>-<slug>`) that cannot collide.
avoid: Re-using a current id in archive/: the resolver cannot tell superseding from superseded doc, so `:supersedes:` fails exactly where it is needed.
Deleting a doc to fix a duplicate; preserving history is the point.
Copying a template doc without changing its `:doc-id:`.
unless: Generated output beneath `docs/dist/` is never scanned.
Docs with no `doc-id` belong to `planner.docs.identity-required`; only declared ids are compared.
why: Uniqueness makes doc-id an identity, not a label, so every edge resolves to one target; a duplicate leaves `:supersedes: architecture.foo` unable to say which `architecture.foo` it means.
evidence: The docs_capability validator reports no duplicate `:doc-id:` across every authored .adoc beneath docs/ (archive/ included, docs/dist/ excluded).
For any archived/replacement pair, the two docs carry distinct ids and the replacement declares `:supersedes:` pointing at the archived id; neither document was deleted.

Reviewer fix example (from source): give the archived document a distinct id and link the succession explicitly:
  docs/architecture/shared-control-root.adoc
    :doc-id: architecture.shared-control-root
    :status: current
    :supersedes: archive.2025-control-root

  docs/archive/2025-control-root.adoc
    :doc-id: archive.2025-control-root
    :status: superseded
verifier_detail: Scope: every authored `.adoc` beneath `docs/`, across all areas, excluding `docs/dist/`. Uniqueness is global — `archive/` is NOT a separate id space. Checked over the whole corpus, not only touched files.
Report EVERY file carrying a duplicated id, not just the second one: there is no principled basis for calling one of them the original.
Only compare ids that were actually declared; documents with no `:doc-id:` are skipped here (reported by planner.docs.identity-required).
audit: Source references: spec 2 §5.1 (uniqueness as precondition for edge resolution); spec 2 §5.2 calls the distinct-ids + :supersedes: shape load-bearing for #1782; spec 2 §2 *Out of scope* (preserving history, no deletion).

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
